title: The Bridge Before I Named It
style: Reflective pop-rock in D minor at 124 BPM, male lead vocal, steady driving rock groove with punchy live drums, melodic electric bass, clean electric-guitar arpeggios and restrained distorted guitars opening into broad choruses. Start intimate and measured, build through the verses with subtle keys and layered guitars, then widen the chorus with stacked harmonies and full-band lift; create a brief stripped-back bridge before a decisive final chorus and resolved instrumental ending. Expressive, connected vocal phrasing, nuanced rather than forceful, polished organic band mix with clear vocal focus.
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I wore a name that fit like an old coat
A Catholic childhood, left unbuttoned
Brothers taught us every life had worth
And faith could make a neighbor out of anyone

I learned the poor were not a footnote
That science didn’t cheapen what we see
I let the miracles go quiet
Kept a small account of guilt and gratitude for me

[Pre-Chorus]
I found a flaw in every proof
For heaven and for its absence too
So I stood where neither side could claim me
Calling that the honest thing to do

[Chorus]
I said I wasn’t an atheist
I said the fence was where I belonged
Then one April page made plain to me
The words I’d carried had been wrong
My faith had thinned to human kindness
No sacred answer underneath
I crossed the bridge before I named it
And finally called myself what I believed

[Verse 2]
On the seventeenth I wrote it down
A title in Spanish, searching for a shape
I thought I’d only make my case
Instead the old explanation slipped away

Not Christian hope, but hope in people
Not a hand above the turning years
The God who stepped into our history
Wasn’t one I could confess as real

[Pre-Chorus]
I pressed publish, watched the sentence leave
Then understood what I had done
It wasn’t just a change of label
It was the ending of the one I’d worn

[Chorus]
I said I wasn’t an atheist
I said the fence was where I belonged
Then one April page made plain to me
The words I’d carried had been wrong
My faith had thinned to human kindness
No sacred answer underneath
I crossed the bridge before I named it
And finally called myself what I believed

[Bridge]
A new white robe, a name announced
Rome turned pages in the spring
For a moment I could almost picture
Staying where the language fit
But a gentler voice can’t turn a bridge around
Once your feet have crossed the span

[Final Chorus]
I said I wasn’t an atheist
I thought the fence would hold me long
Then one April page made plain to me
The words I’d carried had been wrong
My faith had thinned to human kindness
And nothing else I had to keep
I crossed the bridge before I named it
Now I can say what I believe

[Outro]
No thunder, no grand sign
Just a sentence, and a line
The bridge was crossed
And I was mine
